newsitem.title: UK: Saudi crude price cuts drive oil markets down.
newsitem.headline: Saudi crude price cuts drive oil markets down.

text.p: Oil markets weakened on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia, the world's leading producer, cut crude oil selling prices and traders in Europe and the United States struggled to find homes for abundant crude.

Saudi Arabia lopped between 10 and 50 cents off a barrel of crude for worldwide deliveries in May, underlining the general weakness in oil markets, which have seen values fall more than $6 a barrel since the year began.

May futures for benchmark crude oil Brent Blend in London dipped below the psychologically important $19 figure when dealing began, recovered slightly to hover in the range of $19.03-$19.08 a tonne, and then lost their grip after the Saudi news.
Values wobbled below $19 in late afternoon activity.
"Traders will be focusing on the key $19 level to see if there is any support for the market," said energy analyst Leslie Nicholas at GNI Limited.
Brokers had earlier hesitated over the significance of stock data from the United States that showed a big build-up of crude since last week.

American Petroleum Institute (API) data issued after the market closed on Tuesday showed an 11 million barrel rise in crude stocks, which Wednesday's figures from the government's Energy Information Agency confirmed.

Crude markets had already slumped on Tuesday after Shell confirmed its Nigeria operations had returned to normal after tribal disputes blocked production last week and threatened to hold back supplies.
Shell's 950,000 barrels a day (bpd) of Nigerian crude output was running only 50,000 bpd below capacity on Tuesday compared to a 210,000 bpd shortfall last week.
In Europe, spot values for North Sea crude were pinned to the floor under the weight of ample April supplies, traders said.
Cargoes changed hands at depressed values in lacklustre trading.
